effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative descriptive trends and cross-sectional OLS reduced-form regression estimates on aggregated DHS (2003–2013 for infrastructure) and Afrobarometer (2012) data.
effect_estimate.value: Between 2003 and 2013, national mean household access rose from .2 (20%) to .5 (50%) for improved sanitation and from .4 to .6 for potable water, while ethnic horizontal inequality (GGini by geopolitical zone) declined from .3 to about .1 for improved sanitation and from .15 to .05 for potable water. In cross-sectional OLS regressions across LGA-ethnic state units (N = 631; Table 4), precolonial political centralization in compliant (non-supermajority Muslim) ethnic states is positively associated with historically federally administered flush toilet access (beta = .059, SE = .026, p < .05; baseline without interaction beta = .039, SE = .019, p < .05), whereas noncompliance/hegemonization under the 1976 Local Government Reform Law (Cent x Supermajority Muslim interaction) offsets this gain (beta = -.055, SE = .029, p < .10). In contrast, for locally administered WASH services (N = 631; Table 5), neither precolonial centralization nor Cent x Supermajority Muslim is statistically significant for improved pit latrines (Cent beta = .008, SE = .045; Cent x S.Mus beta = .007, SE = .064; Supermajority Muslim beta = .181, SE = .065, p < .01), piped water (Cent beta = .014, SE = .037; Cent x S.Mus beta = .033, SE = .038), or tubewell water (Cent beta = .079, SE = .060; Cent x S.Mus beta = -.104, SE = .066). Across LGAs matching 2012 Afrobarometer and 2013 DHS data (Table 7), local government trust and quality are positively associated with locally administered improved pit latrines (trust in local governing council beta = .127, SE = .072, p < .10; cleaning beta = .132, SE = .048, p < .01; health standards beta = .170, SE = .054, p < .01; marketplace maintenance beta = .183, SE = .058, p < .01), negatively associated with federally administered flush toilets (trust beta = -.214, SE = .052, p < .01; cleaning beta = -.124, SE = .049, p < .05; health beta = -.141, SE = .050, p < .01; marketplace beta = -.193, SE = .044, p < .01), and not significantly associated with piped water (betas -.019 to .030, p > .10).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <= 2 for cross-sectional observational design; rated 1 because the study documents reduced-form statistical associations (explicitly noted by the author as correlations) between historical centralization/1976 Local Government Reform compliance proxies, perceived local government quality, and WASH access without directly observing fiscal/administrative allocation transactions.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines federal-local administrative division of WASH responsibilities across federal government and 774 LGAs (institutional_fragmentation), bilateral political bargaining and compliance/rebellion between ethnic state leaders and federal regimes under indirect rule and the 1976 Local Government Reform Law (political_coordination), and discretionary federal infrastructure allocation/withholding vs. local government quality substitution (discretion).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Quantitative observational analytical study estimating cross-sectional OLS regressions on pooled DHS averages (1990–2013 / 2003–2013) across LGA-ethnic state units and single-wave 2012 Afrobarometer / 2013 DHS LGA cross-sections without a quasi-experimental comparator (no DiD, IV, RDD, ITS, or panel FE; author explicitly describes estimates as correlations). Historical-institutional context informs variable construction, fitting JBI Analytical Cross Sectional appraisal.

sample_size.comment: Uses five Nigeria DHS waves (1990, 2003, 2008, 2010, 2013; adults aged >= 18; infrastructure available in 2003–2013 waves) and the 2012 (and 2008) Afrobarometer surveys, aggregated spatially rather than reporting total individual respondent N in the main text. Exact analytical sample sizes reported in tables are at the LGA-ethnic state and LGA levels.
sample_size.value: 685 LGA-ethnic state units with available DHS and Murdock data (out of 1,415 partitions across 774 LGAs and 61 of 117 ethnic states): N = 678 LGA-ethnic states in infrastructure summary statistics (N = 685 for education), N = 631 LGA-ethnic states in main infrastructure OLS regressions (N = 638 for education); N = 135–171 LGAs / LGA-ethnic units in 2012 Afrobarometer summary statistics and N = 127–162 centralized LGA-ethnic units in split-sample trust regressions (individual respondent N from 1990–2013 DHS and Afrobarometer waves not reported in main text)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 12, Table 1; PDF pp. 15–18, Section 5.4 and Tables 2–7

study_design.comment: Combines repeated cross-sectional descriptive inequality indices (GGini, Gini, McKenzie wealth index) across DHS survey rounds with cross-sectional reduced-form OLS regressions of aggregated spatial units informed by Nigerian colonial and postcolonial historiography.
study_design.value: Observational repeated cross-sectional survey inequality analysis (DHS 1990–2013 across 6 geopolitical/ethnic zones) combined with cross-sectional reduced-form OLS spatial regressions at the LGA-ethnic state and LGA levels informed by historiographical institutional analysis
study_design.where_found: PDF pp. 3–6, Sections 1, 3.1–3.2; PDF pp. 8–19, Sections 5.2–5.5, Equation (3)
